name: Nose slimming clip

card.summary: A nose slimming clip is a small silicone or plastic pressure device worn on the nose bridge or tip with the aim of making the nose look narrower, straighter or more lifted.
card.aka: nose shaper, nose lifter, nose straightener
card.note: Plastic surgeons quoted in coverage say clips cannot reshape adult bone or cartilage, and warn about skin injury, especially in teens or after surgery.

quick.overview:
Nose slimming clips are over-the-counter devices that apply external pressure to the nose. Marketing describes them as a no-surgery way to narrow the bridge, straighten or lift the tip, usually in a few minutes a day or overnight.

Similar appliances have a long history, including 19th- and early-20th-century brass and metal nose shapers. Surgeons quoted in articles say adult bone and cartilage are not reshaped by external pressure; testimonials online are mixed and anecdotal.
quick.how: Users place the clip or insert according to the product's own instructions, often for short daily sessions or overnight. Some combine it with nose massage or taping routines.
quick.risks: Surgeons quoted in articles warn about skin irritation, bruising, interference with a developing teenage nose, and displacing grafts after rhinoplasty. A Johns Hopkins plastic surgeon was quoted warning that a small clip could become lodged in the nose and lead to infection.

lead: Nose slimming clips, also sold as nose shapers or nose lifters, are small plastic, silicone or metal appliances worn on the nose to apply gentle pressure. [1] Makers describe them as non-surgical ways to slim the bridge, lift the tip or straighten a nose, and they are priced from a few dollars to about fifty. [1]

People use them in the hope of a refined profile without a rhinoplasty, typically through brief daily wear or overnight use. [1] Plastic surgeons quoted in consumer and clinic coverage generally say that adult nasal cartilage and bone are not remodelled by external clips, and that any visible change is temporary. [1]

The idea has precedent: brass and leather nose shapers such as the Zello-Punkt, patented in 1894, were sold in pharmacies and hairdressers, and a 1907 US patent describes a metal shaper worn at night. [2][3]

chain: A clip or shaper presses on the sides or tip of the nose
Soft tissue is compressed while worn
Users hope for a slimmer, straighter or lifted nose profile
angle.text: Makers market the clip as a way to narrow or lift the nose. Users wear it briefly or overnight, and some report a short-lived tidier look while it is on.

paras: A surgeon's overview lists several product types: an insert worn inside the nostrils with plastic legs that extend to the sides, base and bridge of the nose, marketed as working in three minutes a day; clip-style devices priced around $7.50; and straighteners priced near $50. [1] Some products are advertised as alternatives to surgery with no recovery. [1]

The Zello-Punkt Model 21, patented by Professor G. von Eck in 1894, was a brass nose-shaped appliance with a leather cushion and head band, worn at night and sold through hairdressers and pharmacies. [2] A US patent for a 'Nose-shaper' by Ignatius Nathaniel Soares, filed in 1905 and granted in 1907, describes a lined metal clip with a tongue under the nose tip. [3]

Dr. Sam Rizk, a facial plastic surgeon, states that devices of this kind do not work and cautions about bruising, scarring, infection and effects on a growing teen nose. [1] The author of a historical article on the Zello shaper doubted that it achieved lasting change. [2]
No studies found. Studies in the medical literature on 'nose clips' concern unrelated uses such as breathing tests, exercise-induced bronchoconstriction and nosebleed compression, not shape change.

timeline.event: Zello-Punkt nose shaper patented by von Eck. [2]
Soares files a US patent application for a nose-shaper. [3]
